subject: QBR: roadmap variance, runway asks and contingency
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Cc: Julia Moreno <julia.moreno@cloudops.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: roadmap variance, runway asks and contingency

Team — attaching the QBR runway heatmap (v3) and a short contingency playbook. I pulled together a condensed readout for the product/eng portion of the QBR deck and flagged the items we should call out in the exec readout. High level:

Summary (TL;DR)
- We are tracking 3 material timeline variances that change projected GA windows by 2–6 weeks for prioritized launches (RBAC, Streaming API scaler, and Embed search rerank).
- The primary driver is test coverage gap + delayed infra optimizations for streaming under long-sequence workloads.
- We have mitigation lanes that require either a short feature freeze for non-blocking enhancements or a targeted augmentation of QA and SRE support for two sprints.

What I want from leadership (asks)
1) Approve up to 2 sprints of redirected QA/SRE headcount for critical-path features (cost estimate attached).
2) Confirm whether we should present a revised GA window in the QBR (recommended: show original commitment + downside scenario with contingency).
3) Sign off on enabling the contingency playbook (fallback models and degraded feature set) for customer-facing canaries.

Roadmap variances (details)
- RBAC (authz): integration tests for cross-tenant role propagation are failing intermittently under quota stress. Impact: potential 2–3 week slip if we require full regression. Proposed mitigation: parallelize tests + temporary narrowed scope for first public rollout.
- Streaming API scaler: kernel selection on p99 paths causes tokenization thrash; infra patch landed but needs validation at scale. Impact: 3–6 week slip if throughput doesn't stabilize. Proposed mitigation: short-term vertical autoscale for demo cohorts + extended burn-in.
- Embed rerank: model quantization quality regressions in A/B are small but visible; requires one more tuning cycle. Impact: 2 weeks. Proposed mitigation: hold on quantization rollout for rerank and fallback to FP16.

Attached: qbr_runway_heatmap_v3.xlsx (sheet: heatmap + risk lanes), contingency_playbook_v1.pdf
Drive link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QBR-Runway-Heatmap
Jira reference: SUP-2143 (streaming scaler validation)

Suggested slide framing for QBR (30–45s each):
- Slide A: consolidated heatmap with two scenarios (on-track / downside)
- Slide B: top 3 risks + action owners and ETA for mitigation
- Slide C: ask slide (resource approval, freeze decision, fallback activation)

Operational notes
- If leadership approves the redirected QA/SRE, Aditya can start reassignments by EOD Wed.
- If we show revised windows, I recommend being explicit about customer impact and what we will do to reduce risk post-QA ramp.

Open items / decisions needed by Wed EOD:
- Resource redirect approved? (Monica)
- Freeze window: Do we impose a hard freeze next sprint except for critical fixes? (Vivek + Laura)
- Contingency activation for canaries? (Leadership)

Thanks — I will update the heatmap and the deck fragments after decisions.

—
Monica Patel
Head of Product Operations | Redwood Inference
monica@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0183


From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: roadmap variance, runway asks and contingency

Monica — thanks for the clear synthesis and the attachments. Quick responses: 

1) Approve redirecting QA/SRE for up to 2 sprints but require a short cost-and-impact note (projected $K and what deprioritized work looks like) before we commit the headcount. Please include the expected reduction in slip probability per mitigation lane.

2) For the QBR, show both the original commitment and the downside scenario. I agree with your framing — we should be explicit, own the variance, and show a concrete mitigation timeline.

3) Approve enabling the contingency playbook for canaries (limited to internal and early-adopter cohorts) but do not activate broad public fallback until we validate the patch on the streaming scaler.

Action items for owners:
- Aditya: produce the cost/impact note and ETA for QA/SRE reassignment by EOD Wed (11 May).
- Monica: update the deck slides with the two-scenario framing and a short embedded note on customer messaging (due Thurs noon).
- Laura: be prepared to speak to customer communications and SLA implications in the QBR.

I'll block 20 minutes on Thurs for a final readout before the QBR prep run.

Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
CEO | Redwood Inference
vivek@redwood.com

Thanks — short note: I support the redirected QA/SRE for two sprints for the critical-path items. We should tie the resource ask directly to the OKR risk metric (reduce risk of GA slip from medium->low) so we can report progress in the QBR. I will add a slide that maps the top 3 variances to the relevant OKRs and the success criteria for mitigation.

I'll coordinate with Aditya to include a quick before/after gating checklist that we can show in the exec pack. Monica — if you send the heatmap with the updated ETA numbers I will slot the OKR mapping slide into the deck ( Thurs COB ).

Neha
Neha Kapoor

neha@redwood.com
